title: Scripts
description: data/scripts.json -- the scripts of the project as the export writes them, read by lib/calc-engine.typ (find-calculation's `script` branch, so #val("x", domain: ("script", "<id>")) and #show-calc("script", "<id>") both reach one; docs/domain/scripts.md §3.3sexdecies, v0.100). One entry per Woodcore-Datei/scripts/<id>.py, carrying the {vars, steps, checks, results} shape every calculation of this engine has (section 2 rule 2) -- `steps` and `checks` are always empty, a script declaring values and not a working. A script that failed is exported all the same, with `calculated: false` and its reason, so the report refuses to print what it names rather than the export stopping (the v0.33 rule).

schema_version.description: -- pinned: a record written at another version is refused rather than read as this one.

scripts.description: One entry per script, keyed by its id, which is its file name without the .py.

id.description: The file's name without its suffix, and the string the report addresses it by.

name.description: Its @name, the id where it carries none.

label.description: Its @label: the description, "" where it carries none.

group.description: Its @group: the folder of the tab's left pane, "" for the root.

calculated.description: Whether the run produced results. false where it failed, timed out or declared none -- `reason` says which.

reason.description: Why nothing was produced, "" where it ran through. How long the run took is not recorded: a wall-clock duration would differ at every export, where data/ must stay unchanged to the byte when nothing else changed (docs/conventions/build-and-release.md §12).

vars.description: The results the script declared, one var each, in the shape section 3.1 defines. `norm` and `norm_ref` are "" where the script cites nothing: what a script computes is the engineer's own arithmetic, so `source` names the file that produced it (`python:scripts/<id>.py`, section 2 rule 5) and there is no normative citation to invent. A report that wants one states it at the call -- #val(..., norm: "SIA 265") -- which is what val's own override is for.

symbol.description: Typst math source (section 6bis): the name itself where the script states none.

steps.description: Always empty: a script declares values, not a working.

checks.description: Always empty: a verification is written in the report with #verify.

results.description: The names of the vars, in the order the script declared them: what show-calc prints at level 1.
